summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of SiO2 using tris(dimethylamino)silane (TDMAS) and ozone. TDMAS dissociatively adsorbs on Si(100) surfaces, forming hydroaminocarbons and Si hydrides, even at room temperature. Ozone oxidizes the adsorbed TDMAS, making the surface active for further TDMAS adsorption, completing the ALD cycle. The process occurs at room temperature and relies on OH sites generated by H2O adsorption.
evidence: TDMAS dissociatively adsorbs on the Si(100) surface to produce adsorbates including hydroaminocarbons and Si hydrides even at room temperature. Ozone oxidizes TDMAS adsorbed on the Si surface and makes the surface active to further TDMAS adsorption to progress the ALD cycle.
